plan.goal: Generate runnable PuLP code to solve a Product Mix optimization problem that maximizes total profit subject to resource capacity constraints (Machine A, Machine B, Labor, Raw Material) and demand constraints (Min Production, Max Market Demand) for 50 products.

tasks.description: Analyze the production dataset to confirm the problem structure. Identify that this is a Product Mix / Production Planning problem. Note that the dataset provides per-unit resource requirements but does NOT include total available capacity for Machine A, Machine B, Labor, and Raw Materials. Recommend reasonable capacity assumptions (e.g., total capacity = mean requirement * 1.5 * number of products, or set as parameters to be easily adjustable). Return: (1) Problem type confirmation, (2) List of decision variables, objective function, and constraints, (3) Recommended capacity assumptions with justification.
tasks.expected_output: A structured analysis document containing: problem type (Product Mix LP), decision variables (production quantity for each of 50 products), objective (maximize sum of profit_per_unit * quantity), constraints (resource capacity limits for Machine A, Machine B, Labor, Raw Material; min/max production bounds per product), and recommended capacity values with rationale.

tasks.description: Based on the data inspection, formulate the complete mathematical model and prepare the data structures needed for PuLP. Specifically: (1) Define the objective function: Maximize Z = sum(Profit_Per_Unit[i] * x[i] for all products i). (2) Define resource constraints: sum(Machine_A_Hours_Req[i] * x[i]) <= Capacity_A, sum(Machine_B_Hours_Req[i] * x[i]) <= Capacity_B, sum(Labor_Hours_Req[i] * x[i]) <= Capacity_Labor, sum(Raw_Material_Units_Req[i] * x[i]) <= Capacity_Raw. (3) Define demand constraints: Min_Production_Requirement[i] <= x[i] <= Max_Market_Demand[i] for each product. (4) Specify the recommended capacity values to use. Return: Complete mathematical formulation with all coefficients and capacity values clearly stated.
tasks.expected_output: Complete mathematical model specification including: objective function formula, all constraint formulas with numerical capacity values, variable bounds, and a clear mapping of data columns to model components. This will serve as the blueprint for code generation.

tasks.description: Generate complete, runnable Python code using the PuLP library that solves the Product Mix optimization problem. The code must: (1) Import pulp and pandas. (2) Load the CSV data (tmpgf1ociws.csv). (3) Define the LP problem as a maximization problem. (4) Create decision variables x[i] for each product with bounds [Min_Production_Requirement, Max_Market_Demand]. (5) Set the objective function as the sum of Profit_Per_Unit * x[i]. (6) Add four resource constraints using the recommended capacity values from the analysis. (7) Solve the problem and print: optimal production quantities for all products, total profit, and resource utilization (slack/surplus for each constraint). (8) Include clear comments and make capacity values easily adjustable as parameters at the top of the script.
tasks.expected_output: A complete, well-commented Python script that loads the CSV, builds the PuLP model, solves it, and prints the optimal solution with all relevant details. The code must be runnable as-is and produce meaningful output.

tasks.description: Review the generated PuLP code for correctness and completeness. Check: (1) All 50 products are included as decision variables. (2) Objective function correctly maximizes total profit. (3) All four resource constraints are properly formulated with correct coefficients. (4) Min/Max production bounds are correctly applied. (5) The code is syntactically correct and would run without errors. (6) Output includes all necessary information (quantities, profit, utilization). Return: Validation report with pass/fail for each check and any suggested fixes.
tasks.expected_output: A validation report listing each correctness check with pass/fail status and any issues found. If issues are found, provide specific code corrections needed.

"""
Product Mix / Production Planning Optimization Model
====================================================
This script solves a linear programming problem to maximize total profit
subject to resource capacity constraints and market demand bounds for 50 products.

Capacity assumptions are based on a 1.5x multiplier of mean requirements as recommended.
"""

import pandas as pd
from pulp import (
    LpProblem,
    LpMaximize,
    LpVariable,
    lpSum,
    LpStatus,
    value,
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Configuration & Data Loading
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CSV_PATH = r"C:\Users\simon\AppData\Local\Temp\tmpgf1ociws.csv"

# Recommended capacities (1.5x multiplier of mean requirements)
CAPACITY_MACHINE_A = 128.33
CAPACITY_MACHINE_B = 150.54
CAPACITY_LABOR = 250.67
CAPACITY_RAW_MATERIAL = 756.0

# Load dataset
df = pd.read_csv(CSV_PATH)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Model Definition
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create maximization problem
prob = LpProblem("Product_Mix_Optimization", LpMaximize)

# Decision variables: production quantity for each product
# Using Continuous variables to ensure feasibility; change to "Integer" if discrete units are strictly required.
x = {
    row["Product_ID"]: LpVariable(
        f"x_{row['Product_ID']}",
        lowBound=row["Min_Production_Requirement"],
        upBound=row["Max_Market_Demand"],
        cat="Continuous",
    )
    for _, row in df.iterrows()
}

# Objective function: Maximize total profit
prob += lpSum(row["Profit_Per_Unit"] * x[row["Product_ID"]] for _, row in df.iterrows()), "Total_Profit"

# Resource constraints
prob += lpSum(row["Machine_A_Hours_Req"] * x[row["Product_ID"]] for _, row in df.iterrows()) <= CAPACITY_MACHINE_A, "Machine_A_Capacity"
prob += lpSum(row["Machine_B_Hours_Req"] * x[row["Product_ID"]] for _, row in df.iterrows()) <= CAPACITY_MACHINE_B, "Machine_B_Capacity"
prob += lpSum(row["Labor_Hours_Req"] * x[row["Product_ID"]] for _, row in df.iterrows()) <= CAPACITY_LABOR, "Labor_Capacity"
prob += lpSum(row["Raw_Material_Units_Req"] * x[row["Product_ID"]] for _, row in df.iterrows()) <= CAPACITY_RAW_MATERIAL, "Raw_Material_Capacity"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Solve & Output Results
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
prob.solve()

print(f"Solver Status: {LpStatus[prob.status]}")
print(f"Maximum Total Profit: ${value(prob.objective):.2f}\n")

if prob.status == LpStatus.OPTIMAL:
    print("Optimal Production Quantities:")
    print("-" * 40)
    for prod_id, var in x.items():
        qty = var.varValue
        # Format output: show integer if whole number, else float
        qty_str = f"{int(qty)}" if qty.is_integer() else f"{qty:.2f}"
        print(f"{prod_id}: {qty_str} units")
else:
    print("Warning: The problem could not be solved to optimality.")
    print("Consider relaxing constraints or adjusting capacity assumptions.")

"""
Product Mix / Production Planning Optimization Model
====================================================
This script solves a linear programming problem to maximize total profit
subject to resource capacity constraints and market demand bounds for 50 products.

Capacity assumptions are based on a 1.5x multiplier of mean requirements as recommended.
"""

import pandas as pd
from pulp import (
    LpProblem,
    LpMaximize,
    LpVariable,
    lpSum,
    LpStatus,
    value,
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Configuration & Data Loading
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CSV_PATH = r"C:\Users\simon\AppData\Local\Temp\tmpgf1ociws.csv"

# Recommended capacities (1.5x multiplier of mean requirements)
CAPACITY_MACHINE_A = 128.33
CAPACITY_MACHINE_B = 150.54
CAPACITY_LABOR = 250.67
CAPACITY_RAW_MATERIAL = 756.0

# Load dataset
df = pd.read_csv(CSV_PATH)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Model Definition
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create maximization problem
prob = LpProblem("Product_Mix_Optimization", LpMaximize)

# Decision variables: production quantity for each product
# Using Continuous variables to ensure feasibility; change to "Integer" if discrete units are strictly required.
x = {
    row["Product_ID"]: LpVariable(
        f"x_{row['Product_ID']}",
        lowBound=row["Min_Production_Requirement"],
        upBound=row["Max_Market_Demand"],
        cat="Continuous",
    )
    for _, row in df.iterrows()
}

# Objective function: Maximize total profit
prob += lpSum(row["Profit_Per_Unit"] * x[row["Product_ID"]] for _, row in df.iterrows()), "Total_Profit"

# Resource constraints
prob += lpSum(row["Machine_A_Hours_Req"] * x[row["Product_ID"]] for _, row in df.iterrows()) <= CAPACITY_MACHINE_A, "Machine_A_Capacity"
prob += lpSum(row["Machine_B_Hours_Req"] * x[row["Product_ID"]] for _, row in df.iterrows()) <= CAPACITY_MACHINE_B, "Machine_B_Capacity"
prob += lpSum(row["Labor_Hours_Req"] * x[row["Product_ID"]] for _, row in df.iterrows()) <= CAPACITY_LABOR, "Labor_Capacity"
prob += lpSum(row["Raw_Material_Units_Req"] * x[row["Product_ID"]] for _, row in df.iterrows()) <= CAPACITY_RAW_MATERIAL, "Raw_Material_Capacity"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Solve & Output Results
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
prob.solve()

print(f"Solver Status: {LpStatus[prob.status]}")
print(f"Maximum Total Profit: ${value(prob.objective):.2f}\n")

if prob.status == LpStatus.OPTIMAL:
    print("Optimal Production Quantities:")
    print("-" * 40)
    for prod_id, var in x.items():
        qty = var.varValue
        # Format output: show integer if whole number, else float
        qty_str = f"{int(qty)}" if qty.is_integer() else f"{qty:.2f}"
        print(f"{prod_id}: {qty_str} units")
else:
    print("Warning: The problem could not be solved to optimality.")
    print("Consider relaxing constraints or adjusting capacity assumptions.")
